Chest: Pectoralis major moves the upper arm; pectoralis minor positions the scapula.
Upper Chest: The clavicular portion belongs to pectoralis major.
Back: A region containing several muscles, not one muscle.
Lats: Latissimus dorsi helps extend and adduct the arm.
Rhomboids: Rhomboid major and minor retract and stabilize the scapula.
Shoulders: Includes muscles moving the arm and positioning the shoulder girdle.
Lateral Delts: The middle deltoid contributes to arm abduction.
Rear Delts: The posterior deltoid contributes to arm extension.
Anterior Delts: The anterior deltoid contributes to arm flexion.
Rotator Cuff: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis surround the shoulder joint.
External Rotators: Infraspinatus and teres minor contribute to outward arm rotation.
Serratus Anterior: Moves and stabilizes the scapula against the thorax.
Biceps: Biceps brachii flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm.
Forearms: Contain muscles controlling wrist and finger movement.
Fingers: Movement involves both forearm and intrinsic hand muscles.
Arms: A broad region, not a single muscle.
Lower Back: This region includes posterior trunk muscles that support and move the vertebral column.
Spine: A skeletal region supported and moved by surrounding muscles; it is not itself a muscle.
Core: A training term for trunk musculature, including abdominal muscles. It is not one anatomical structure.
Obliques: Internal and external obliques contribute to trunk rotation and lateral flexion.
Glutes: Gluteus maximus contributes to hip extension; gluteus medius and minimus contribute to abduction.
Hamstrings: Posterior thigh muscles contribute to knee flexion; most also extend the hip.
Quads: The quadriceps group extends the knee. Rectus femoris also crosses the hip.
Hip Flexors: Iliacus and psoas major are important contributors to hip flexion.
Calves: Gastrocnemius and soleus contribute to ankle plantar flexion, pointing the foot downward.
Tibialis Anterior: Contributes to ankle dorsiflexion, lifting the front of the foot, and inversion.
Legs: A broad training region containing multiple muscle groups and joints.
Full Body: A training category, not a single structure. Movement combines the actions of multiple muscles.
Stabilizers: A functional role: muscles can hold a bone steady so another movement can occur.
